posts.title: Inside SantaCon’s beginnings in the ’90s
posts.description: These days, SantaCon is an infamously hated holiday in which thousands of people dress in red and go on a bar crawl. It wasn’t always. SantaCon began in 1994 as pure absurdism, designed to shock people out of their day-to-day by creating a sense of awe and confusion. Occasionally, it got out of hand: Police at some of the early SantaCon events believed them to be a group of terrorists and met them with a wall of officers in riot gear. Read more: Watch the trailer for Dead City Punx doc, made with Zack de la Rocha From director Seth Porges ( Class Action Park, How to Rob a Bank ), SANTACON is a new documentary that uses never-before-seen VHS tapes to take audiences back in time to the original SantaCon events in the ’90s. posts.title: Fan poll: 5 best New Found Glory albums
posts.description: Beginning in South Florida’s hardcore scene, New Found Glory built out a local following by touring around the East Coast while they were still in high school. In 1999, they pooled their money together to record their scrappy debut album, Nothing Gold Can Stay , and got picked up by Drive-Thru. By the early 2000s, they were already a massive voice within pop punk’s mainstream explosion, pairing infectious hooks with blistering energy alongside their peers in blink-182 , Sum 41 , and Fall Out Boy . These days, they’re pretty much the same band, keeping their pop-punk core intact while exploring different impulses over the years, from all-acoustic to piano to heavier alternative rock. That includes this year’s Listen Up! , which was written and recorded while Chad Gilbert underwent chemotherapy (and sadly passed away in September 2026). posts.title: Lambrini Girls release new single benefiting abortion access
posts.description: Lambrini Girls have released their new single, “Don’t Talk to Me Until I’ve Had My Abortion,” from their forthcoming album, No Refunds , out in January via City Slang. The track is a critique of the patriarchal forces determined to police women’s bodies. Alongside the song, they launched a fundraiser in support of ARC Southeast, an independent U.S. reproductive healthcare organization assisting those seeking abortion care. Read more: The Lambrini Girls effect The campaign will run through next week, concluding on Dec. 1 with the premiere of the video for the song. They’ll start the new year with a handful of shows in the U.K. Earlier this month, they announced their Coachella debut next year, after their spring tour in support of No Refunds , with dates in New York City, Toronto, Chicago, and more.
